rule: LOOKS LIKE: Red, green, and blue pieces, a head on a rail, and a striped arm. GOAL: Pick up the pieces in the shown order to build the chain; this level cleared in three arrow moves. CONTROLS: Up and down moved the head along the rail. Right extended the arm; left pulled it back. RULE: Touching a piece SHOULD attach it; pulling back SHOULD carry attached pieces with the arm. TRAP: Thinking the striped arm was a trailing body hid how reaching and pulling worked. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There is no rail or extending arm, or pieces must be pushed rather than picked up.

LOOKS LIKE: A blue piece, a blue outline, corridors, a switch, and a red gate. GOAL: Get the blue piece to the blue outline while a replay holds the switch to open the gate. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece along corridors. Space started the other run and replayed the first; pressing it again reset both. RULE: A piece on the switch SHOULD open the gate, letting one run clear the way for the other. TRAP: Thinking Space would remove the red barrier wasted time; the switch controlled it. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There is no replay run to hold a switch while another piece moves.

LOOKS LIKE: A piece, a target, switches, linked barriers including a red one, and a ghost replaying an earlier run. GOAL: Reach the target using a recorded run to hold a switch and open the way; cleared with fifteen arrow moves and one Space press. CONTROLS: Arrows moved your piece. Space started another run while a ghost replayed your earlier moves. RULE: A piece on a switch SHOULD move its linked barrier; a ghost SHOULD be able to keep the route open. TRAP: Expecting Space to remove the red barrier wasted time. Its switch controlled it. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There is no recorded replay or no switch linked to a barrier.

LOOKS LIKE: A craft in a blocked corridor, green blocks, and a pink marker. GOAL: Guide the craft through the corridor to the pink marker; this level cleared in two arrow actions. CONTROLS: Left and right moved the craft sideways. Clicking a green block removed it without moving the craft. RULE: You SHOULD open a lane, then steer into it; the route advanced automatically. TRAP: Removing all green blocks did not finish the level; the craft still had to travel through the openings. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There is no craft to steer through openings in a blocked corridor.

LOOKS LIKE: Pieces, switches, red and yellow barriers, a goal, and slots for recorded runs. GOAL: Use recorded runs to open barriers, then reach the goal with the final piece. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece. Space saved a run and started the next; after the last slot, it reset the runs. RULE: Ghosts SHOULD replay earlier moves. Red barriers SHOULD need a piece holding their switch; yellow barriers SHOULD stay open after their switch is left. TRAP: Thinking Space always kept useful recordings cost time; cycling past the last slot erased them. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Earlier runs do not replay as ghosts.

LOOKS LIKE: Red, orange, blue, and green pieces, with a rod arm moving along a rail. GOAL: Collect red, orange, blue, then green in that order; this level took nine arrow presses. CONTROLS: Up and down moved the arm along the rail. Right extended it; left retracted it, carrying collected pieces. RULE: You SHOULD collect with the rod tip. Moving the arm vertically pushed loose pieces; carried pieces could push them too. TRAP: I thought orange touching carried red would attach it. Orange joined only when the rod tip reached it. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There is no rod arm that extends from and retracts toward a rail.

LOOKS LIKE: A board with red and purple switches, ghosts, an active piece, a corridor, and an exit portal. GOAL: Leave ghosts on both switches, then take the open corridor to the portal; this clear took three arrow actions. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active piece. Space saved its route and started another run while ghosts replayed saved routes. RULE: A ghost SHOULD hold its switch while the active piece goes elsewhere; reach the portal after both ghosts reach their switches. TRAP: Assuming every arrow press moved wasted a recording: a blocked step left the ghost short of its switch. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Saved routes do not replay as ghosts.

LOOKS LIKE: A craft, green blocks, barriers, a pink marker, and a deadly purple and yellow structure. GOAL: Guide the craft past barriers to the pink marker; level two was cleared in four actions. CONTROLS: Arrows steered the craft; clicks removed green blocks. The clear used three arrow actions and one click. RULE: The craft SHOULD rise automatically through open space; blocks SHOULD act as brakes as well as barriers. Leave some overhead to stop at a safe turn. TRAP: Clearing every block looked helpful, but let the craft rise into the deadly structure. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The craft stays still in open space until moved.

LOOKS LIKE: A horizontal rod, a vertical support, red, orange, blue, and green pieces, and goal marks that light up. GOAL: Collect red, then orange, then blue, then green on the horizontal rod. CONTROLS: Right extended the rod; left retracted it; up and down moved it vertically. RULE: Pieces on the support SHOULD slide off its bottom before the rod carries them away; the frames proved this was needed. TRAP: A lit goal mark did not mean a piece was secured; retracting too soon left it on the support. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no horizontal rod or vertical support.

LOOKS LIKE: A moving piece, ghosts, yellow and red gates, red and purple switches, a portal, and a goal. GOAL: Open yellow gates, leave ghosts holding red and purple switches, then take the portal to the goal. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece; Space saved a nonempty route for a ghost to replay next run. RULE: Yellow gates stayed open; red gates and portals needed held switches. You SHOULD advance ghost replays only through successful moves. TRAP: Wall pushes seemed like waiting but did not advance ghosts. Step away and back instead. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Without ghosts replaying saved routes, the board MAY use different rules.

LOOKS LIKE: A craft, a pink goal, purple hazards, green blocks, and orange tiles that can show open cross marks. GOAL: Guide the craft to the pink goal, opening a safe path around purple hazards; cleared with four arrow actions and one click. CONTROLS: Arrows steered the craft. Clicks removed green blocks or switched orange tiles between solid and open. RULE: The craft SHOULD rise automatically until blocked; solid orange tiles SHOULD act as brakes, and open cross marks SHOULD be safe to cross. TRAP: Thinking an orange cross mark was dangerous led to clicking it again and closing the path. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The craft stays still without arrow input.

LOOKS LIKE: Blue, green, red, and orange pieces, cyan and yellow supports, and a rod threaded through pieces. GOAL: Stack blue above green on cyan, and red above orange on yellow; cleared in seven arrow moves. CONTROLS: Up and down raised and lowered the rod and threaded pieces; right extended it; left withdrew it. RULE: Supported pieces SHOULD stay parked during withdrawal, letting groups separate and stack. Extension through a piece MAY behave differently; the note ends before saying how. TRAP: Assuming every withdrawal dragged every threaded piece left. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There is no rod to thread through pieces or no supports to park them on.

LOOKS LIKE: Red switches, recorded ghosts, yellow gates, yellow connecting lines, an active piece, and a patrol. GOAL: Leave recorded ghosts on the red switches, reach the bottom switch, then return to the goal before moves ran out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the active piece and advanced the patrol; this clear took nineteen arrow moves. RULE: You SHOULD cross through spaces the yellow gates leave open as the patrol shifts them; the return trip needed timed crossings again. TRAP: A switch’s yellow connecting line looked like a corridor, but it was not walkable. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There are no patrol-shifted gates to time your crossings around.

LOOKS LIKE: A board with a rod, movable pieces, and a fixed obstacle. GOAL: Put the pieces into the required arrangement around the obstacle; level five was cleared with thirty arrow presses. CONTROLS: Up and down moved the rod vertically. Left pulled it back; right extended it. RULE: You SHOULD allow for full retraction: the rod could pull back completely, leaving every piece behind. Carrying a piece was not always necessary. TRAP: Assuming the rod had to hold at least one piece ruled out useful moves and wasted time. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There is no rod that moves vertically and extends or retracts.

LOOKS LIKE: A craft, pink target, purple hazards, green blocks, red tiles, and a staircase, with solid floors and ceilings. GOAL: Guide the craft to the pink target without touching purple hazards; level four cleared with one click. CONTROLS: Movement steered sideways; clicking green blocks removed them; activating red tiles reversed gravity. The staircase carried the craft upward. RULE: Gravity SHOULD pull the craft until a solid block stops it; intact floors and ceilings SHOULD provide safe stopping places. TRAP: Flipping gravity near the open entrance seemed safe but sent the craft into purple hazards. Activate beneath an intact ceiling instead. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board lacks a gravity driven craft and solid stopping surfaces.

LOOKS LIKE: A craft, pink target, purple hazards, red switches, green blocks, and orange outlines. GOAL: Guide the craft to the pink target without touching purple hazards. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the craft sideways. Clicks reversed gravity at red switches, removed green blocks, or made orange outlines solid. RULE: You SHOULD use gravity to carry the craft until a solid block stops it; keeping or adding blocks provided safe stopping places. TRAP: Assuming orange controls removed hazards wasted time. They created blocks that could stop the craft before it hit a hazard. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The craft stays still between moves instead of being carried by gravity.

LOOKS LIKE: Solid blocks, orange outlines, red switches, purple floors, and an exit. GOAL: Reach the exit by changing gravity and preparing safe landing blocks; cleared with eight arrow actions. CONTROLS: Arrows moved you; red switches reversed gravity; orange outlines could be filled or cleared to make or remove blocks. RULE: You SHOULD prepare landing blocks before reversing gravity: solid blocks stopped falls, empty outlines did not, and purple surfaces were deadly. TRAP: Blaming the budget for deaths wasted time; the real cause was falling through unfilled outlines onto purple floors. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Gravity stays fixed, or outlines cannot become solid landing blocks.

LOOKS LIKE: Green and yellow sliders with red tips, target markers, and matching colored arrow panels. GOAL: Line up both sliders’ red tips with their target markers; this level was cleared in five clicks. CONTROLS: Green arrows moved the green slider sideways; yellow arrows moved the yellow slider up or down. RULE: You SHOULD count fixed steps, not single spaces; the green right button extended its bar by three spaces. TRAP: Assuming every click moved just one space gave the wrong move count. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board lacks sliders whose red tips must line up with target markers.

LOOKS LIKE: A linked coloured arm with a red tip, a target, a purple wall, and coloured arrow buttons. GOAL: Guide the arm through the gap above the purple wall and line up its red tip with the target; level two took eighteen clicks. CONTROLS: Buttons extended matching segments: orange and yellow right, sky blue up, green down. RULE: Each click SHOULD extend its segment by three spaces and move all pieces attached beyond it. TRAP: Treating coloured pieces as separate sliders hid how an early extension shifted the whole arm. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Pieces slide independently instead of moving as a linked arm.

LOOKS LIKE: Colored bars, white barriers, red markers, and buttons for the bars. GOAL: Clear barriers from both target bars’ paths, then move both onto their red markers; cleared in twenty clicks. CONTROLS: Red lowered a white barrier; orange shifted another right. Blue moved the red assembly left; green lifted the orange assembly. Target bars’ buttons extended their tips. RULE: Attached barriers SHOULD move with their supporting bars; blocked moves SHOULD be refused, as the frames proved. TRAP: Believing nearby colored bars were linked wasted moves; red and orange actually moved white barriers. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board lacks movable bars, barriers, or target markers.

LOOKS LIKE: Five yellow bars, including a central tip, with colored controls and side bars. GOAL: Raise the central yellow tip to its target while keeping the side bars clear; cleared in ten clicks. CONTROLS: Yellow extended or retracted all five yellow bars together. Colored controls raised or lowered the side bars. RULE: You SHOULD check clearance for every yellow bar, not just the central one, because they moved together. TRAP: Treating yellow as controlling only the central tip hid why the side bars needed repositioning first. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The yellow control moves only the central tip rather than all five yellow bars.

LOOKS LIKE: Green and sky blue tips, targets, walls, a moving barrier, and orange, green, blue, and sky blue controls. GOAL: Guide both tips onto their targets while clearing the walls and barrier. CONTROLS: Orange raised or lowered green; green moved it sideways and lifted the barrier; blue shifted the barrier sideways; sky blue extended or retracted its bar. RULE: Linked pieces SHOULD move together; a collision MAY stop the whole move. TRAP: Advancing green with sky blue extended wasted time; retracting sky blue first made room for the barrier to rise. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no linked tips and moving barrier.

LOOKS LIKE: A jointed arm, a target beneath a purple overhang, a gap on the left, colored panels, and buttons above them. GOAL: Guide the arm’s tip through the left gap to the target. CONTROLS: Colored panels extended or retracted matching segments; buttons above them rotated the arm’s joints. RULE: You SHOULD leave clearance for the whole arm: moving a segment also moved the pieces attached to it. TRAP: Trying to reach straight down wasted time; the overhang required a route around its left side. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no jointed arm with attached pieces that move together.

LOOKS LIKE: Colored beads on rods, with one rod active. GOAL: Sort the colored beads into the required color groups. CONTROLS: Click a rod to make it active. Arrow keys move it sideways or extend and retract it. RULE: Beads on the other rod SHOULD stay pinned; beads SHOULD NOT be pushed onto that rod. A blocked sideways push SHOULD stop the whole move. TRAP: Assuming every blocked bead stops extension too. An extending rod can pass through a blocked bead without moving it. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no rods to select, move sideways, extend, or retract.

LOOKS LIKE: Pink and purple rods, two blues, two reds, and a green. GOAL: Put both blues and green on pink’s rod, and both reds and green on purple’s rod. CONTROLS: Click a rod to select it; use arrows to move it. RULE: Green MAY count for both rods. Level seven SHOULD be solvable: it cleared in nineteen actions, fifteen arrows and four clicks. TRAP: Assuming green can belong to only one rod. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no selectable rods or no pink and purple target rods.

LOOKS LIKE: Colored arm ends, matching targets, narrow gaps, extension panels, rotation buttons, and a red barrier with a red control. GOAL: Guide the colored arm ends onto matching targets while fitting through narrow gaps; Level 7 cleared in three clicks. CONTROLS: Extension panels lengthened or shortened sections; rotation buttons turned sections and everything beyond them; the red control turned the red barrier. RULE: You SHOULD expect a turn to move the whole attached chain; shortening folded sections first MAY help through tight spaces. TRAP: Treating the red barrier as fixed wasted time searching for a route around it. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no linked arm sections to extend or rotate.

LOOKS LIKE: A purple block, a dotted route, a white cross marking a stop, and a blue circle. GOAL: Move the purple block along the dotted route to the blue circle; level one was cleared in five clicks. CONTROLS: Click the white cross to move the block onto it, then click farther along the route. RULE: You SHOULD use the marked stopping point rather than try to jump straight to the goal. TRAP: Believing that clicking the blue circle or the purple block would start movement; neither did. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no dotted route or marked stopping point.

LOOKS LIKE: A green marker, a yellow target, red and blue bridges, and red and blue buttons. GOAL: Guide the green marker to the yellow target by arranging a connected path. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the marker two spaces; the red button turned the red bridge; the blue button switched which blue bridge was solid. RULE: You SHOULD use only solid, connected bridges to carry the marker. TRAP: Assuming the blue button rotated the whole mechanism instead of switching bridge states. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no bridges to turn or switch between solid states.

LOOKS LIKE: Small colored blocks and a blue goal; clicks target nearby spots. GOAL: Merge the small pieces into one final block, then move it into the blue goal. This level took four clicks. CONTROLS: Click nearby spots to move pieces toward them; clicking the goal alone does nothing. RULE: Matching pieces SHOULD merge into the next color when they meet; clicks SHOULD have limited reach. TRAP: Believing a click between two blocks would pull both together; it moved only the nearer one. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no colored pieces to merge or no blue goal for the final block.

LOOKS LIKE: A board with a green marker, yellow target, bridges, red and blue controls, and a small red floor control. GOAL: Reach the yellow target by connecting the bridges. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the marker two spaces. Red turned its bridge; blue switched which blue crossing was solid. The small floor control needed a visit, not a click. RULE: You SHOULD cross solid bridges and stand on a fixed pivot when turning a bridge beneath you. TRAP: Assuming every coloured control worked remotely wasted time; the small red control had to be reached on foot. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no bridges to connect or turn.

LOOKS LIKE: A board with coloured blocks, including cyan, magenta, purple and yellow, and blue goals. GOAL: Make one yellow block and one purple block, then deliver each to its own blue goal; cleared in five clicks. CONTROLS: Click near pieces to draw them toward the click; move blocks with short steps. RULE: Matching pieces SHOULD merge into the next colour: cyan, magenta, purple, then yellow. Keep one purple aside. TRAP: Believing a distant goal click would pull a block all the way there wasted clicks; movement had limited reach. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Clicking near pieces does not draw them toward the click.

LOOKS LIKE: A green marker, yellow goal, bridges, pink pads, purple routes, colored tokens, and colored controls. GOAL: Guide green to yellow using bridges, pink pads, and the purple route. CONTROLS: Arrows moved two spaces; red rotated its bridge; blue switched solid crossings; pink teleported between pads; purple activated purple paths after unlocking. RULE: You SHOULD use only solid paths; frames proved they supported movement. Collecting a colored token unlocked its control. Fixed bridge pivots SHOULD be safe places to rotate. TRAP: Thinking blue rotated a bridge wasted time; it switched which crossings were solid. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There are no solid paths, colored tokens, or matching controls.

LOOKS LIKE: Eight cyan pieces, a pink hazard symbol, and a goal. GOAL: Combine all eight into one yellow piece and place it in the goal. Level four cleared in five clicks. CONTROLS: Clicking pulled nearby pieces toward that spot. Reset restored the starting layout. RULE: Matching colours SHOULD merge: cyan into magenta, magenta into purple, purple into yellow. The pink hazard SHOULD move after clicks and weaken pieces it reaches. TRAP: Treating pink as harmless wasted a run. Save exposed pieces first and merge away from it. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Pieces do not pull toward clicks, or matching colours do not merge.

LOOKS LIKE: A marker, an exit, upper and lower bridges, two moving platforms, and yellow, gray, and pink pads. GOAL: Reach the exit across the upper bridge, using moving platforms and restoring the lower bridge. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the marker. Yellow shifted both platforms right, then back left. Gray extended one bridge while shortening the other. Pink pads teleported between each other. RULE: You SHOULD expect platforms not to carry the marker, and shifts leaving it unsupported to be refused. Walk between safe shifts. TRAP: Assuming a moving platform would carry you wasted time. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Platforms carry the marker as they move.

LOOKS LIKE: A board with blocks, hazards, and color swatches used as a legend. GOAL: Merge matching blocks into the goal block while keeping enough material safe from hazards; this level took seven clicks. CONTROLS: Clicks moved and merged blocks; reset restarted the level. Color swatches were not controls. RULE: You SHOULD expect hazards to pursue blocks, not empty clicks, and their attacks to downgrade blocks; the frames proved this. TRAP: Clicking empty space to lure hazards away wasted turns while they attacked the blocks. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Hazards chase empty clicks, or color swatches act as controls rather than a legend.

LOOKS LIKE: Red and pink blocks, separate goals, and color swatches; orange and yellow appear as red changes. GOAL: Turn the red block yellow, then place yellow and pink in separate goals; cleared in four clicks. CONTROLS: Click to pull nearby pieces toward that spot. Reset restarts the level. Color swatches are only a legend. RULE: Pink contact SHOULD lower red to orange, then yellow, as shown. Pink also moved toward colored blocks. TRAP: Believing clicks repelled pink wasted time; the final test showed nearby pieces were pulled toward the click. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Clicking pushes nearby pieces away instead of pulling them closer.

LOOKS LIKE: Yellow goal, purple token and paths, movable bridges, pink teleport pads, orange object, claw, white rail, colored buttons, and small platform. GOAL: Reach yellow after collecting purple, moving bridges, and using pink pads; cleared with one arrow action. CONTROLS: Arrows moved you; small arrow buttons moved claw; red gripped or released orange; colored buttons switched paths; gray moved small platform. RULE: Claw SHOULD follow white rail; you SHOULD stand directly on pink to teleport and use small platform to switch safely between purple paths. TRAP: Treating white rail as walkable wasted time; it carried claw, not you. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board lacks the rail carried claw and pink teleport pads.

LOOKS LIKE: A board with coloured blocks, pink splitters, two goals, and colour swatches serving only as a legend. GOAL: Fill both goals with yellow blocks, using merges for one and pink splitter contacts for the other. Level seven cleared in two clicks. CONTROLS: Click to pull nearby blocks and pink splitters toward the click. Reset starts the level over. RULE: Merges SHOULD raise block colour: red becomes orange, then yellow. Splitter contact SHOULD lower it. TRAP: Thinking clicks pushed pink away wasted moves; nearby pink splitters follow clicks too. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Clicks push nearby pieces away rather than pulling them closer.

LOOKS LIKE: A board with yellow, pink, red, orange, and green pieces, goals, and colour legend swatches. GOAL: Put two orange pieces and one green piece on goals; this level was cleared in three clicks. CONTROLS: Click near movable pieces to steer them. Faraway clicks and legend swatches did nothing. RULE: Two yellows SHOULD merge into orange; two pinks SHOULD merge into green. Pink contact SHOULD lower red to orange, but could lower orange again. TRAP: Thinking green came from pink touching a block wasted time; green actually came from merging two pinks. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Matching yellow or pink pieces touch but do not merge.

LOOKS LIKE: Two rows of five switches, yellow objects, a blue center, and a reset control. ESTABLISHED: Switches SHOULD change while yellow objects SHOULD stay fixed, as the frames showed. The level remains uncleared. FAILED: Visiting every switch setting and testing blue center clicks across multiple settings produced no clear. GOAL IS NOT: Simply cycling through all switch settings. No winning condition has been confirmed. CONTROLS: Each switch toggled its own bit. Blue center clicks had no visible effect. The reset control’s effect was not recorded. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board lacks switches that toggle independently.

LOOKS LIKE: An orange and blue block, a white cross, and a chamber marked with a blue symbol. GOAL: Move the orange and blue block onto the white cross; this level was cleared with seven arrow moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block in five-cell steps in the chosen direction. RULE: You SHOULD treat the fixed white cross as the target: the block moved while the cross stayed put. TRAP: Assuming the blue-symbol chamber was the exit wasted moves; it blocked entry. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The target moves with the block, or arrows do not move the block in five-cell steps.

LOOKS LIKE: A block carrying a symbol, a marked exit, a cross, yellow rings, and a move bar along an edge. GOAL: Turn the carried symbol to match the exit, then reach it before the move bar runs out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block one step; entering the cross turned its symbol a quarter turn. RULE: Three cross entries SHOULD give the needed match here; yellow rings SHOULD refill the bar. Each stretch MAY allow about twenty-one moves. TRAP: Treating yellow rings as teleporters wasted time; they refilled the bar without moving the block. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Yellow rings move the block elsewhere instead of just refilling its move bar.

LOOKS LIKE: A symbol block, a colored directional exit, white-edged passages, a multicolor tile, a cross, and yellow tiles. GOAL: Reach the exit with the symbol matching its color and direction before the move budget runs out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block through passages and onto special tiles. RULE: You SHOULD expect the multicolor tile to change color, the cross to turn the symbol, yellow tiles to restore the budget once each, and white-edged passages to carry the block straight to their far ends. TRAP: Thinking a used yellow tile would refill the budget again wasted a return trip. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There is no exit requiring matching color and direction.

LOOKS LIKE: A block carrying a coloured shape, coloured tiles, a white transformation tile, white edge strips, an exit, and limited moves. GOAL: Reach the exit carrying its matching colour and shape before moves run out; this level took fifteen arrow moves. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block; special tiles changed its symbol, refilled moves, or triggered transport. RULE: You SHOULD expect colour tiles to cycle colours, the white transformation tile to change shape, and white strips to transport away from the strip along its row or column. TRAP: Assuming every white strip sent the block downward caused loops and wasted moves. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There is no carried symbol to match to an exit.

LOOKS LIKE: A board with a movable block, an exit, special tiles, a rotation cross, and a red zigzag symbol with an extra detached square. GOAL: Bring the exit that matching symbol before moves run out; this level cleared with one arrow move. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block; special tiles changed its symbol, refilled moves, or transported it. RULE: You SHOULD track the cross through a four-step cycle; it advanced only when the block moved successfully. TRAP: Treating the cross as fixed made a planned pair of visits produce only one rotation. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no movable symbol block or matching-symbol exit.

LOOKS LIKE: A craft among ledges, passages, hazards, and a goal, with side controls and red and orange controls; the view scrolls. GOAL: Guide the craft through the upper opening, down the outer shaft, and onto the goal without hitting hazards. CONTROLS: Side controls moved left or right; red reversed gravity; orange placed a brake. RULE: You SHOULD expect gravity to carry the craft until a ledge or brake stops it; brake height determined which passage it could enter. TRAP: Mistaking camera scrolls for moving terrain hid the true connections between passages. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: There is no gravity-driven craft or no way to place a brake.

LOOKS LIKE: A block, red and blue destinations, shape tiles, turn tiles, and move budget refill tiles. GOAL: Reach red, then blue, carrying the matching shape and facing the required way each time; cleared in fifteen arrow moves. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block; shape tiles changed its form, turn tiles rotated it, and refill tiles restored its move budget. RULE: You SHOULD count six shape families and expect a form change to keep the current facing. TRAP: Assuming only five forms, or that changing shape reset facing, caused wrong predictions and wasted moves. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The piece has no facing or destinations do not require matching shapes.

LOOKS LIKE: A craft, solid blocks, a goal chamber with a roof and entrance, and a red switch. GOAL: Guide the craft across the chamber’s roof and open its entrance to get inside. CONTROLS: Click blocks to change the path; click the red switch to reverse gravity; use arrows to move sideways. RULE: You SHOULD build a landing before reversing: gravity keeps carrying the craft until a solid block stops it. TRAP: Reversing gravity does not stop the craft at the goal; without a landing, it falls past the entrance. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The craft stops freely in open space instead of continuing under gravity until blocked.

LOOKS LIKE: A blue and yellow craft, green blocks, solid shelves with gaps, a pink goal, a bottom bar, and a pointer. GOAL: Get the craft up through the gaps to the pink goal. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows steered sideways; clicking a green block removed it. RULE: The craft SHOULD rise automatically until blocked. The bottom bar MAY show moves remaining. TRAP: Assuming green blocks only stop upward travel; they also blocked sideways entry. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Pieces swap places to make matching rows instead of clearing a path for a rising craft.

LOOKS LIKE: Red, green, and blue blocks beside a pink base with a checkered arm; a bottom edge bar shows the colour order. GOAL: Touch red, then green, then blue to clear the level. CONTROLS: Up and down shifted the base and arm; right extended the arm and left retracted it, in six-cell steps. RULE: You SHOULD follow the bottom colour order. Retracting MAY help avoid touching a later colour too soon. TRAP: Thinking the arrows steered a moving pink head wasted time; the checkered part was an extending arm, not a trail. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Arrows move a free cursor instead of shifting or extend

LOOKS LIKE: Black corridors, a blue block, a blue outlined goal, a red gate and control, a gray replay block, and a bottom bar. GOAL: Get the blue block to its outline beyond the red gate. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; SPACE restarts it and changes the recording or replay phase. RULE: You SHOULD record a trip to the red control, then replay it while taking the gate route; the control opened the gate. TRAP: SPACE did not simply switch between two independent blocks; pressing it again erased the gray replay. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Switching pieces leaves both freely controllable, with no record

LOOKS LIKE: A maze with a blue block, gray replay blocks, red controls and gates, a blue destination, and a shrinking bottom bar. GOAL: Use two recordings to hold two controls, then guide the final blue block to the destination. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block. Space restarts it and begins replaying the recorded route. RULE: You SHOULD expect recorded routes to repeat and hold controls open; blocked moves do not advance the replay. TRAP: Treating Space as a switch between freely controlled characters wasted time; old detours also entered recordings. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: The board has no record

LOOKS LIKE: A craft below green block shelves and tunnels, purple and yellow hazards, and a pink goal above. GOAL: Reach the pink goal through safe gaps without rising into hazards. CONTROLS: Left and right steer the craft; clicking a green block removes it. RULE: You SHOULD keep overhead blocks as brakes until aligned with a safe opening; clearing overhead space lets the craft rise. TRAP: Assuming sideways moves always work wasted time: green blocks beside the craft also blocked entry. DOES NOT APPLY WHEN: Removing overhead blocks leaves the craft still and you must steer upward yourself.

LOOKS LIKE: Corridors with a blue block, gray replays, coloured controls, matching gates, and a blue destination. GOAL: Reach the destination using recorded routes to hold two red controls and toggle a yellow gate. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block. Space restarted it and changed recording or replay mode.
